name: ecommerce-invoices-and-documents-api
description: HTTP adapter over the invoicing domain: documents frozen at issue, numbered per series, corrected rather than edited, delivered as recorded facts, and kept for as long as retention says.
features: The merchant is derived from the credential and is never accepted in a path, a query string or a body
There is no PUT, PATCH or DELETE on a document anywhere: an issued document is corrected by a credit note and discarded by a void that records
A refusal is a fact in the response body, carrying the domain's own reason as the error code, never a bare status
The refusal table is a match over the domain's enum, so a reason added to the domain fails static analysis here rather than arriving as a 500
Three delivery refusals are published as not resubmittable because the attempt row is written before the transport is asked, so the reference is already spent
A document belonging to another merchant, one belonging to another buyer, one whose buyer was erased and one nobody minted are all the same 404 with the same body
No idempotency key: every write already has a natural key the database enforces, and a key a client holds is a key a client can change
A rendition with no renderer bound answers 200 with rendered false and the reason named, because the document is still entirely readable
Money leaves as minor units, an ISO 4217 code, an exponent and a decimal string, and no endpoint accepts or returns a float
No database key ever leaves: a document is named by its reference, because the host published its primary key as an invoice number
Erasure and export are person-wide across every tenant, so they are gated on invoicing:platform-privacy and not on a merchant's ability
An erasure answers 200 with complete on its face, naming every document retention refused, its number and the date the window ends
Two abilities are split by whose documents they reach, and the self-only one cannot name a subject even if an endpoint asked
No listing of numbering series and no pagination: the domain publishes neither query, and both are recorded as gaps rather than improvised here
OpenAPI 3.1 kept in parity with the router in both directions, including the ability each operation enforces
